pr_title: Add support for multicast IPv4 TTL and IPv6 hop limit
pr_body:
Add option support for adjusting the IPv4 multicast time-to-live value. Add also tests for both unicast and multicast TTL settings.
Add also similar IPv6 hop limit option for both unicast and multicast IPv6 packets + tests.
Add checks and tests for IPv4 TTL 0 or IPv6 hop limit 0 when sending packet, the packet should dropped in this case.

Fixes #60299
pr_comments: As a general note, I originally planned to implement the multicast TTL/hoplimit support only, but noticed that the IPv4 TTL and IPv6 hoplimit were a bit flaky, so the changes are more extensive. We were also missing tests for unicast versions, those + multicast ones are now implemented.
Minor tweaks to kconfig file. Added also info to migration guide.
Release and migration note changes in this version.

issue_context.title: Set time-to-live for Multicasts
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
As mentioned in https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/53587 I implemented a Multicast / socket connection to receive Multicasts send via UDP by a client software running on a PC and I send back UDP packages to the client software as an answer to the received packages.

The _time-to-live_ of the package send back is set to 64. I guess that is due to the initial configuration `NET_INITIAL_TTL` set at `zephyr/subsys/net/ip/Kconfig.ipv4`. This configuration is set for the IPv4 interface. I am using only one interface.

I want to reduce the TTL for the multicast / socket connection. I checked `zsock_setsockopt` and the available options, but did not find any matching. 

Is there a possibility to set the TTL for the multicasts, e.g. like the IP_MULTICAST_TTL option described at https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/ip.7.html?

I am using:
- Zephyr v3.1.0
- Toolchain Zephyr SDK
- STM32H747 DISCO Board
comments:
There is currently no way to set a custom TTL for IPv4 multicast packets. At the `net_context` level there is a `net_context_set_ipv4_ttl()`, but the `ipv4_ttl` field it sets is applied for both, unicast and multicast packets.
It'd be needed to:
* Add a new field, `ipv4_multicast_ttl` to the `net_context` structure,
* Add getter/setter function to the `net_context` API
* Implement `IP_MULTICAST_TTL` that makes use of above
* And finally, update `net_context_create_ipv4_new()` to differentiate between unicast/multicast destinations
Also, it's a feature request, not a bug, so changing the label.

review_comments:
there are quite a few of these `net_context_get|set_*` functions (existing ones, and the ones you added) that are missing doxygen comments. Could you please add them? Should these be considered internal (I have no idea myself :)) you may consider not having the doxygen documentation (although it's always nice to have imo), and simply enclose them in ` @cond INTERNAL_HIDDEN` sections.

Sorry that I didn't notice earlier as I really just paid attention to the migration guide changes when the bot added me.
This is a public API change, I think you should leave `net_ipv6_set_hop_limit` in, simply calling `net_if_ipv6_set_hop_limit` and add a deprecation warning.
would be nice to have doxygen comments here as well (again, unless this is something you want to hide from the public API).
Sure, I will submit a follow up pr adding more comments. Thx!
Did you not introduce generic getter/setter function to be used here?

For the ttl and hoplimit getters I did not, the `get_uint8_option()` expects user to supply uint8_t value but the value for the ttl and hoplimit is typically int, so the values were incompatible. Then I thought about creating `get_int_option()` but because we are storing ttl and hoplimit as uint8_t the function was not that nice looking. I will investigate this option getter/setter dilemma in separate PR that I mentioned in the refactoring patch.
While re-checking the PR, I noticed that this test is in wrong commit. I will move it to proper one in next version.
